meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa - International Company jurisdiction regulated by the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) under the Ministry of Finance
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (Westminster-style parliamentary statutes; Samoan custom law applies separately to land and chiefly titles)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Independent State of Samoa for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (signed 2018; in force 2019)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus) (signed 14 June 2017; in force 13 December 2020)
WTO membership of Samoa (acceded 10 May 2012) as the principal trade-law framework; no separate China-Samoa bilateral investment treaty is in force as of 2025

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987, as amended to 2025 (including the beneficial-ownership amendments effective 1 January 2019, obligating each International Company to keep a confidential UBO record with its SIFA-licensed registered agent and to file UBO data to SIFA on demand); International Companies Regulations 1988; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018 (Act No. 23 of 2018), as amended, being the primary AML/CFT statute (customer due diligence, record retention, and suspicious transaction reporting); Samoa International Financial Authority Act 2018 (SIFA as company registry and AML/CFT supervisor for international companies); Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit within the Central Bank of Samoa; Income Tax Act 2012 (offshore exemption regime rendering qualifying International Companies tax-exempt).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passports and Citizenship Office (Samoa) or the passport authority of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarized certified copy; origin-state Hague Apostille accepted where the origin state is an Apostille Contracting Party, noting Samoa is not itself an Apostille party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and financial standing confirmation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Conduct or police clearance certificate for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police authority or Ministry of Justice of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (apostilled or consularized origin certificate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal applicant (signed before a notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarized signature and sworn declaration)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (apostilled corporate extract following a clear origin-state chain of certification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, UBO, and authorized signatory against (i) the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit / Central Bank of Samoa domestic PEP list, (ii) the UN Consolidated Lists, (iii) the OFAC SDN List including CAATSA targets, (iv) the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, and (v) open-source adverse-media and negative-news checks. Screening is electronic with a database audit trail, repeated at least every 90 days during onboarding; any hit triggers enhanced due diligence and immediate escalation to the SIFA-designated compliance officer. Positive PEP status requires senior-management approval for the appointment. For this Low_Risk_Standard medical-device OEM with Swift LC and TT Wire settlement rails, a low-risk score is expected, yet the complete screening trail must be retained for 5 years under the AML/CFT Act 2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) - International Companies Registry name-clearance desk and online eRegistry module (official government portal under the Ministry of Finance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be rendered in Latin (Roman) script using English or Samoan spelling. Chinese-character or other non-Latin names are permitted only as an additional transliterated or foreign-language registered name recorded in the constitution; the Latin-script name remains the sole legal name for all filings, contracts, and Swift LC / TT wire banking documentation. A romanized transliteration and, where applicable, a pinyin or Samoan rendering must be filed simultaneously. No name may create confusion with an existing registered name or imply a connection to the Government.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal (unless authorized by the appropriate authority)
Samoa (requires consent of the relevant Minister)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A filed name is screened by the SIFA Registry for distinctness and prohibited tokens. If rejected, the licensed registered agent may, within 14 business days of the rejection notice, submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar with a revised name and supporting memoranda. The Registrar must determine the request within 5 business days. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Minister responsible for International Companies within 30 days; the appealed name retains a priority hold pending the ministerial decision. A successful appeal directs the Registrar to reserve the name. Each resubmission or one additional 30-day extension attracts the statutory clearance fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual-office-only is prohibited for International Companies. A physical registered office in Samoa and a SIFA-licensed resident registered agent are mandatory under the International Companies Act 1987. A virtual mailbox may be used only as a supplementary address and cannot serve as the registered office or as the place where statutory registers, UBO records, and accounting records are kept.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10%-15% in the first 12 months for a new low-risk trading or manufacturing-holding International Company. Inspections are normally conducted through the registered agent, but SIFA may conduct unannounced inspections of agent premises at a higher frequency of approximately 25%-35% per annum. The Company must be able to produce, within 48 hours, its statutory registers, UBO file, and AML/CFT records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), including sections on incorporation (ss. 5-9), share capital and subscribers (ss. 10-12), registered office and registered agent (ss. 13-15), and directors and officers (ss. 18-22).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with the Application for Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued with the consideration determined by the directors. No escrow account or capital deposit is required under the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED NO. 1: The share subscription details set out in the Memorandum and Articles of Association are approved and adopted, and each subscriber is recorded as a shareholder effective on incorporation. RESOLVED NO. 2: The registered office at [Samoa address] and the appointment of [registered agent] as registered agent are confirmed and shall be maintained at all times. RESOLVED NO. 3: The holders of the following offices are appointed to manage the company: ________ as Director and ________ as Secretary. The board authorises the issue of share certificates, adoption of the common seal, and opening of bank accounts. Any one director or secretary may execute documents on the company's behalf. The resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the SIFA online portal to submit a proposed company name and obtain clearance. Confirm that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered international company, local company, or protected trademark.
required_dossiers: Proposed memorandum and articles of association draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised company name within 5 business days together with a written explanation; the Registrar will re-adjudicate within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Statutory Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent or local legal counsel on behalf of the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987. Have the incorporator(s) execute the instruments and provide a notarised certificate of execution if required. The registered agent must endorse acceptance of its role.
required_dossiers: Consent and appointment of registered agent
Consent of first director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the content or signature, amend the instruments by written resolution of the incorporators and resubmit within 7 days; no re-notarisation is required if the correction is typographical.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Office of the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the signed incorporation application, memorandum, articles, and statutory declarations to the Registrar, either online or by courier. Pay the gazetted government filing fee of USD 250 and any commission of the licensed registered agent.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Incorporation of an International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing information, the registered agent files a response within 10 business days. If the fee is insufficient, the Registrar issues a deficiency note; payment must be settled within 5 business days or the application is deemed withdrawn.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Governance Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar. Register the company's registered office and registered agent details. Prepare the initial board resolution, minutes of the first board meeting, share register, and statutory records in the company's registered office.
required_dossiers: Registered office and registered agent confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is issued with errors, apply to the Registrar for rectification under the International Companies Act 1987, providing a copy of the original certificate and affidavit of corrections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Trade and Manufacturing Section

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report required for manufacturing activities involving vapour deposition, handling of cesium iodide, and electronic waste generation; categorised as a prescribed activity under the Planning and Urban Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Samoa's environmental discharge standard limits normally aligned with the World Bank Group General EHS Guidelines (temperature, pH 6-9, COD, TDS, heavy metals). Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must be controlled through exhaust scrubbing and monitoring; hazardous solid waste, including solvent wastes and electronic scrap, must be stored and removed by licensed waste contractors in accordance with the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification must be obtained from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) before occupation. Structural load inspections for cleanroom and heavy equipment installations must be certified by the Ministry of Engineering and Infrastructure. Occupational health clearance and workplace safety audit, including radiation safety and chemical handling, are required from the Labour and Employment Relations Division of MCIL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) – official portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Samoa International Companies ('ICs') incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from Samoa income tax and do not receive an income tax TIN. Where an IC undertakes taxable or zero-rated supplies under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2008, it must apply for VAGST registration with the SRA using Form VAGST-REG. Application requires certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office details, director particulars, and forecast taxable turnover. Optional voluntary registration is permitted when only zero-rated exports are made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime. An International Company may elect into tax-exempt status at incorporation; deregistration or conversion to a domestic company triggers full taxability. No alternative entity classification elections are available under Samoa law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) – VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 taxable supplies in any 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance is in force. SRA does not currently operate API-based digital stamping. Taxpayers must issue sequential tax invoices respecting VAGST Act 2008 Section 46 and retain records for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Samoa by the supplier or on behalf of the supplier, with export occurring no later than 14 days after the date of supply; services supplied to a non-resident recipient where the benefit is wholly or partly outside Samoa; and internationally transported passengers or goods. Input VAT on direct and apportionable overhead related to zero-rated exports may be refunded through the SRA quarterly VAT refund filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD-1) audited by Samoa Customs
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing foreign currency receipt
Original commercial invoice and zero-rated VAGST tax invoice
Copy of export contract or purchase order
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA may disallow zero-rating and issue a formal assessment for VAGST underpaid, plus an automatic late payment penalty of 25% of the unpaid tax. Fraudulent or false export claims carry an additional 50% penalty, a fine up to WST 100,000, and imprisonment for up to five years. SRA may reopen assessments for up to five years from the filing date, or indefinitely in cases of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) as the exchange control authority acting under the Exchange Control Act 1975, the Exchange Control Regulations 1976, and the Financial Institutions Act 2007
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa tala (WST) is not a fully convertible international currency. Current account transactions generally receive unrestricted conversion through authorized dealers, but capital account transactions are subject to CBS exchange control approval or exemption. A Samoan International Company (IC) classified as a non-resident offshore entity may hold and operate foreign currency accounts in USD, AUD, NZD, EUR, or JPY at licensed commercial banks without mandatory conversion into WST. Dividend distributions and repatriated capital to non-resident shareholders are structurally smoother when the IC maintains its full treasury in USD or AUD because no WST conversion is required at the operating-bank level; profit remittance hurdles arise only if the IC converts offshore receipts into WST for local Apia operating costs. CBS approval is advisable before any large shareholder loan repayment, capital reduction, or liquidation distribution, and the underlying transaction evidence must demonstrate that the flow is a genuine trade or capital transaction rather than a disguised domestic financing arrangement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident Samoa exporters must bring export receipts through an authorized dealer and surrender for conversion into WST within 30 days of receipt unless a CBS exchange control exemption or foreign-currency retention account has been approved. For the WS_IC International Company structure, the mandatory surrender ratio is effectively zero where the entity is designated as non-resident and holds a CBS-approved foreign-currency account; all proceeds from export sales of vapor-deposited amorphous silicon cesium iodide DR detectors may be retained in USD or AUD. The IC should nevertheless maintain a documentary trail of export invoices, airway bills or bills of lading, customs declarations, and proof of payment to satisfy the six-month export proceeds realization rule, which requires that Samoan exports be paid for within 180 days from shipment unless an extended term has been approved by CBS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Foreign Currency Account
Operational Foreign Currency Account / Trade Finance Account
Capital Escrow Account / Local Currency Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Samoa has no dedicated electronic-money institution or digital-bank licensing category; an entity seeking to issue e-money or provide payment services must obtain a restricted or full licence from the Central Bank of Samoa under the Financial Institutions Act 2007, which effectively requires a physical Samoa presence and a substantial AML/CFT compliance function. Offshore global EMI providers such as Wise or Airwallex generally do not offer onboarded USD or WST accounts to Samoa International Companies due to de-risking by correspondent banks and limited Pacific routing capabilities. The only feasible structure is a local bank-backed white-label arrangement where a licensed Samoan commercial bank holds the underlying funds and the EMI merely provides a restricted cross-border interface. Legal risks include unlicensed money transmission, exchange control infringement, and repudiation by the AML/CFT supervisor; therefore, the IC should treat foreign digital EMIs as auxiliary payment rails only after obtaining a written legal opinion from a Samoa counsel confirming that the EMI does not engage in deposit taking or money transmission in Samoa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoa CBS AML/CFT rules do not expressly mandate physical attendance by directors, but the risk-based CDD approach requires account opening to be completed through an appointed representative, director, or senior officer with verified identity. In practice, at least one director or the Samoa resident company secretary may be required to attend a branch interview at ANZ or BSP before operational foreign-currency accounts are activated. Remote video onboarding is permitted by some banks if accompanied by notarized corporate documents and an approved correspondent-bank opinion, but the board is recommended to provide in-person presence in Apia for the first EC-KYC meeting to eliminate underwriting delays. The KYC file must include the original or certified certificate of incorporation, registered-agent certificate, board resolution for account opening, source of signatory authority, passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, a pre-approval funds-source questionnaire, and a brief narrative of the digital X-ray flat-panel manufacturing value chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident offshore company without visible economic substance, flagged as high-risk due to International Company status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-agent compliance certificate, current annual return from the Samoa International Companies Register, notarized board resolution, physical office lease or work-station agreement in Apia, payroll evidence for resident officers or directors, audited financial statements or management accounts, detailed organizational chart, and an operational narrative showing that the IC is the procurement and distribution hub for vapor-deposition DR detector components.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of capital injection identified as intercompany transfer from a related party in a higher-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreement, board approval for capital contribution, source-of-funds letter from the remitting shareholder's principal bank, six months of bank statements of the shareholder with explanation for large deposits, certificate of incumbency of the shareholder entity, ultimate beneficial owner passport and tax identification number, and SWIFT MT103 referencing the precise purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected sanctions exposure or controlled goods concern relating to X-ray detector and scintillator materials
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UN sanctions clear-screening report for all counterparties, end-user undertaking and end-use certificate confirming non-military hospital diagnostic use, export control classification analysis for amorphous silicon panels and cesium iodide crystals, downstream distributor due diligence files, restricted-party screening of customers and suppliers, and comprehensive supply-chain documents including purchase orders, proforma invoices, shipping invoices, and customs HS codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient commercial justification for outbound trade disbursements to component suppliers and potential trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master OEM supply agreement for vapor-deposition detector production, supported by invoice level 3-way matching, purchase order, packing list, logistics booking notes, custom declarations, goods-receipt signed by the off-take hospital distributor, and a workflow report showing the physical flow of digital X-ray panels. The dossier should also contain insurance certificates and photographs of finished medical products to prove the underlying medical-technology trade is real and value-consistent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The preferred compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 from the parent or subscribing shareholder's bank to the Samoa IC's foreign-currency capital escrow account held at ANZ Bank Samoa Limited or Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited. The wire instruction must identify the beneficiary as the International Company with its full name and Samoa company registration number; the remittance information field should contain a precise purpose declaration such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION FOR SHARE SUBSCRIPTION — WS_IC ISIC 3250' or 'INVESTMENT IN EQUITY OF SAMOA INTERNATIONAL COMPANY' to satisfy CBS exchange-control reporting and the receiving bank's CDD. Funds should be transmitted in USD or AUD and held in the IC's offshore-class account without conversion into WST. The receiving bank should be supplied in advance with the certified board resolution, deposit ledger, and a funds-source questionnaire; upon receipt, a foreign-currency credit report is filed with the Central Bank of Samoa in the aggregate periodic returns submitted by the authorized dealer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment of component suppliers, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfer at sight, especially for high-turnover procurements of amorphous silicon substrates, cesium iodide scintillation layers, thin-film transistor panels, and detector read-out electronics. Each outbound instruction should include the underlying invoice number, purchase order, commodity description, HS tariff code, and purpose code for 'Import Payment for Medical Equipment Components'. For larger or repetitive transactions, the Samoa IC may open an irrevocable documentary letter of credit through ANZ or BSP, issued under SWIFT MT700, payable at sight against presenting bank's draft, commercial invoice, clean on board bill of lading, and inspection certificate. Confirming bank capacity in Singapore or Hong Kong is recommended to reduce documentary risk. All outward disbursements must remain within the approved trading threshold and the bank's AML/CFT monitoring framework; reference to the medical X-Ray DR panel end-user and hospital distribution agreement should be kept in the supporting documentation package.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign-exchange forwards between WST and USD, AUD, NZD, or EUR with licensed Samoa commercial banks, limited to underlying trade or capital transactions and a tenor not exceeding 12 months.

Samoa tala non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through a licensed bank's offshore desk where the underlying exposure is supported by contract invoices and CBS approval is obtained where required.
Cross-currency swaps with approved offshore banks for matching long-term project liabilities in USD and functional income receipts, strictly without speculative positions.

Natural hedge strategy by denominating all supplier purchase contracts and customer sale invoices in USD and maintaining a matched USD nostro balance, thereby avoiding WST conversion and reducing the need for derivative instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of International Company (combined with annual government registry fee payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; standard fee tier applies for authorized capital up to USD 1,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee after the 30-day grace period; continued default for 90 days may result in administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register, publication in the Samoa Gazette, and loss of legal status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Agent and Registered Office in Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa (agent maintains records; Registrar is notified by agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the time of filing the annual return, before the anniversary deadline expires
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent and office may cause the agent to resign, triggering a Registrar's show-cause notice and potential strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual No-Tax Status Confirmation (exemption declaration for non-resident international company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (only if a written confirmation is required; no mandatory income tax return for International Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not separately applicable; tax exemption is automatic under the International Companies Act 1987
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No filing penalty applies; failure to maintain good standing under the International Companies Act could jeopardize the statutory tax exemption.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not applicable. Samoa International Companies are exempt from mandatory statutory audit and from filing financial statements, regardless of turnover, assets, or number of shareholders. A court-ordered or shareholder-requested audit may be undertaken voluntarily.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting framework. Voluntarily prepared financial statements may follow IFRS, Samoa equivalent to IFRS, or another generally accepted accounting standard agreed by the registered agent and directors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain and retain a current beneficial ownership declaration from each director and significant shareholder at every annual renewal. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members, and the registered agent must update the UBO register and any related AML/CFT customer due diligence records. The UBO register is not publicly filed but must be available for lawful inspection by the Registrar or Samoa authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 600 per year (standard licensed agent fee including registered office and nominee director services, if any)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (no statutory audit required); voluntary audit for a small radiology hardware holding entity typically costs USD 2,000 - USD 4,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies (tax-exempt offshore regime); standard resident corporate rate: 25%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption for International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987; no capital gains tax; no exchange control restrictions; no stamp duty on offshore transactions; no estate or gift tax on offshore assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Declaration (Form 10) filed with the Registrar of International Companies via the Samoa e-Registry portal, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). No corporate income tax return is required because the IC is tax-exempt.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual government fee falls due on the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the unique IC registration number exactly as shown on the certificate of incorporation.
Must exactly match the certificate of incorporation; no trading names allowed.
Provide the full address of the registered office maintained by a licensed Samoa registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and license number of registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The appointed Samoa-licensed agent must be identified.
List all directors with residential addresses; non-resident individuals or corporate directors are permitted.
Disclose registered shareholders and, where requested, ultimate beneficial owners to the Registrar or FIU; nominee shareholders must be flagged.
Certify that the IC has not carried on business with Samoan residents and has not owned real property in Samoa.
If no business has yet commenced, declare dormant status; if active, briefly state the offshore commercial purpose.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of WST 200 plus WST 50 per month of continuing default; the Registrar may strike off the company, publish a dissolution notice, and charge restoration costs of up to WST 500 plus court fees; directors may be disqualified.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an International Company to its non-resident shareholders under the International Companies Act 1987; no Samoan dividend withholding tax applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: International Companies are tax-exempt entities and ordinarily cannot claim Samoa DTA benefits. Where a treaty reduction is sought under one of Samoa's limited DTAs (e.g., Australia, New Zealand), the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate from the Ministry of Revenue, submit it together with a signed Form 4 (Declaration of Beneficial Ownership) to the paying agent before payment, and establish that it has no permanent establishment in Samoa.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For exempt ICs, royalties and interest derived from outside Samoa are taxed at 0%. Samoa domestic law imposes 15% withholding tax on Samoan-source interest and royalties paid to non-residents; under applicable DTAs the rate may be reduced to 10% for royalties and 10-15% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory transfer pricing documentation is imposed on tax-exempt International Companies. If an IC carries on a taxable onshore business in Samoa (a violation of IC status), the Income Tax Act 1974 applies the arm's length principle and TP documentation obligations are expected to follow OECD TP Guidelines; a Local File / Master File is triggered when annual turnover exceeds WST 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not maintain BVI-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, an International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa, appoint at least one licensed registered agent, keep adequate financial records at the registered office, and avoid deriving income from any Samoan-source activity. The board must hold meetings in person or by proxy at intervals set in the bye-laws, and major related-party transactions require written board approval.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an International Company as a mere conduit while actually carrying on business with Samoan residents, deriving Samoan-source income, or failing to disclose beneficial ownership to the Registrar for the purpose of exploiting the IC tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 1974 and the International Companies Act 1987, the Commissioner may re-characterise the IC as a resident taxable company, impose corporate income tax at 25% on unreported Samoan-source profits, add monthly interest at 1%, and levy penalties up to 150% of the tax avoided. The company may be struck off and its assets frozen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties; the court may order civil recovery of diverted profits, impose travel bans, and impose imprisonment of up to 7 years for wilful tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no board activity, no real registered office (only a mailbox), no accounting records, and no legitimate offshore commercial purpose; using the entity solely to hold assets in a non-transparent manner and refusing to provide beneficial ownership information to the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike off and dissolve the company; the FIU may impose administrative fines of up to WST 100,000; assets may be restrained under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2004; the separate legal personality of the shell company may be disregarded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold nominee directors personally liable for all company obligations; directors may be disqualified for up to 10 years, subjected to personal bankruptcy proceedings, and charged with criminal offences that may trigger extradition.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payment rails (SWIFT LC, TT Wire) through the International Company without conducting customer due diligence, using bearer shares or opaque nominee arrangements, or failing to file suspicious transaction reports (STRs) with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit in the course of high-value medical equipment contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2021, failure to comply attracts a fine of WST 500,000 for a corporate body and WST 100,000 for an individual; the company's registration or operating licence may be revoked; Samoa may be subjected to international countermeasures and blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal liability of up to 5 years' imprisonment, personal financial penalties, disqualification, freezing of bank accounts by the Central Bank of Samoa, confiscation of proceeds, and travel bans pending investigation.
